title: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay with a Salary Sacrifice Car Australia Guide
description: Learn how to convert hourly pay to annual salary using the 38-hour week. Includes tax, super, and salary sacrifice car Australia options for 2026-27.
salarySummary: Annual gross pay is your hourly rate × 38 hours per week × 52 weeks, assuming a standard full-time week.

faqs.q: How does salary sacrifice car Australia affect my annual pay calculation?
faqs.a: Salary sacrifice car Australia arrangements reduce your pre-tax salary in exchange for a vehicle. This lowers your taxable income but does not change the hourly rate used in the annual conversion. The calculator on [the timesheet](/) assumes no salary sacrifice, so you should adjust your expected annual gross by subtracting the sacrificed amount before applying tax. Super is still calculated on your ordinary earnings, which may be reduced if the sacrifice is made from pre-tax salary.

faqs.q: What tax brackets apply to my annual salary in 2026-27?
faqs.a: For 2026-27, the resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy is generally 2%. These rates apply to your taxable income after any salary sacrifice car Australia deductions. Use [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) estimates to see your net income.

faqs.q: Is superannuation paid on top of my annual salary?
faqs.a: Yes, super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This means your total employment cost is higher than your annual gross. Salary sacrifice car Australia contributions can also be made from pre-tax salary, but the 12% super is calculated on your ordinary time earnings before any sacrifice. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Hourly Pay to Annual Salary

If you earn an hourly wage or are considering a salary offer, the standard conversion uses a 38-hour week and a 52-week year. The formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 = annual gross salary**. This article explains the calculation, the role of the National Minimum Wage, casual loading, superannuation, and how a **salary sacrifice car Australia** arrangement can affect your figures.

### The Basic Formula

For a full-time employee working 38 hours each week, the annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026), the annual gross is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44. This assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. The fortnightly pay is simply the weekly pay multiplied by two: $26.44 × 38 × 2 = $2,009.44 before tax.

If you work different hours, adjust the hours per week in the formula. The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool on this site lets you enter your own hours.

### Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

The National Minimum Wage is set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** into the timesheet; instead, use the base rate and tick the casual loading checkbox.

Award rates vary by industry and occupation. They are higher than the minimum wage and include specific penalty rates, allowances, and overtime. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award. If you are covered by an award, your hourly rate may be different from the minimum.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. For the minimum wage example, the super contribution would be $52,245.44 × 12% = $6,269.45, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional cost to the employer. When comparing salary offers, remember that your total employment cost includes super. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more on salary sacrifice.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross is not what you take home. Tax is deducted using the 2026-27 resident rates:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- Above $190,000: 45%

Plus a 2% Medicare levy (based on 2025-26 single reduction thresholds as 2026-27 thresholds were not confirmed). For the minimum wage example, the annual tax would be approximately $5,092 plus Medicare, leaving a take-home pay of around $45,000. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a precise estimate.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many Australian employees are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly gross by two. For a $30 per hour rate at 38 hours: weekly = $1,140, fortnightly = $2,280. This is useful for budgeting and comparing with salary offers that are often quoted annually or fortnightly.

### Salary Sacrifice Car Australia

A **salary sacrifice car Australia** arrangement allows you to use pre-tax income to pay for a vehicle, reducing your taxable income. This does not change your hourly rate or the annual gross calculated from it, but it lowers the amount subject to tax. For example, if you sacrifice $10,000 per year, your taxable income becomes $42,245.44 instead of $52,245.44, saving you tax at your marginal rate. Super is still calculated on your ordinary earnings before sacrifice, so your super contributions are unaffected. Always check with your employer and the Australian Taxation Office for eligibility and fringe benefits tax implications.

### Average Weekly Earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) for full-time adult ordinary time as $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). This is an average across all industries and states, not the median for any specific job. The all employees total earnings average is $1,579.20 per week, which includes part-time workers. These figures can help you benchmark your salary, but your actual pay depends on your award, enterprise agreement, or individual contract.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed calculations, visit [the timesheet](/) to enter your hourly rate, or check [reference tables](/data) for tax and super rates.
